introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Computer Science 2 (0595), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2019. Duration: two hours.**

Answer any FIVE questions. All questions carry 20 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators or Phones are NOT allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the meaning of the following terms used in project management.

(i) Predecessor task (2 marks)

(ii) Critical path (2 marks)

(iii) Slack time (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Predecessor task (2 marks).** A predecessor task is a task that must be finished (or at least started, depending on the dependency) before another task, called its successor, can begin. Example: the foundations must be built before the walls.

**(ii) Critical path (2 marks).** The critical path is the longest sequence of dependent tasks from the start to the end of a project. It gives the shortest time in which the whole project can be completed, and a delay in any task on it delays the whole project.

**(iii) Slack time (2 marks).** Slack time (also called float) is the amount of time by which a task can be delayed without delaying the following tasks or the completion date of the project. Tasks on the critical path have zero slack time.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A teacher intends to present a lecture to students in a hall using a computer application software.

(i) State the most appropriate Application Software that can be used. Give one reason for your choice. (2 marks)

(ii) Name any three hardware devices that can be used alongside the computer to facilitate the teacher's lecture in the hall. (3 marks)

(iii) Name two other Application Software that can be used to prepare the lecture. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Most appropriate software (2 marks).** **Presentation software** (for example Microsoft PowerPoint or LibreOffice Impress), 1 mark. Reason (1 mark): it lets the teacher prepare slides that combine text, pictures, charts and animation and show them one after another to a large audience.

**(ii) Three hardware devices (3 marks, 1 mark each).** Any three of: a **multimedia (data) projector**, a **projection screen**, a **loudspeaker or public address system**, a **microphone**, a **wireless presenter (remote control and pointer)**, an interactive whiteboard.

**(iii) Two other application programs (2 marks, 1 mark each).** Any two of: a **word processor** (lecture notes and handouts), a **spreadsheet** (tables and charts of data), **graphics or image-editing software** (diagrams and pictures), video or audio editing software.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Give two differences between an impact printer and a non-impact printer. (2 marks)

(ii) Give an example of each type of printer in c(i). (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Differences (2 marks, 1 mark each).**

| Impact printer | Non-impact printer |
|---|---|
| Forms characters by striking an inked ribbon against the paper with pins or hammers | Forms characters without striking the paper (ink sprayed, or toner fused with heat or laser) |
| Noisy | Quiet |
| Slower, lower print quality | Faster, higher print quality |
| Can print carbon copies (multi-part forms) | Cannot print carbon copies |

Any two differences are accepted.

**(ii) Examples (2 marks, 1 mark each).**

- Impact printer: dot-matrix printer (also daisy-wheel or line printer).
- Non-impact printer: inkjet printer (also laser or thermal printer).

questions.enonce_markdown:
State the role of each of the following in relation to data transmission.

(i) Receiver (1 mark)

(ii) Transmitter (1 mark)

(iii) Protocol (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Receiver (1 mark).** The device that receives the transmitted signals or data, converts them back into a form the user or computer can use, and may send an acknowledgement.

**(ii) Transmitter (1 mark).** The device that sends the data: it encodes the data into signals suitable for the transmission medium and sends them.

**(iii) Protocol (1 mark).** A set of agreed rules that governs how data is formatted, sent, received and checked, so that different devices can communicate (for example TCP/IP or HTTP).
